title: Sangiovese Spine: Chianti Classico, Montalcino & the Pecorino Hills
subRegion: Chianti Classico, Montalcino, Val d'Orcia & Cortona

bestPeriod.avoid: Late July-mid-August, 35-38°C and Ferragosto closures; also 20 Sept-5 Oct, when owners are on the crushpad and answer nothing

food.note: Trattoria mains €14, €22; Cecchini set menus €35, €60; one blowout €120, €180

transport.note: Car 6 days €260, €400, fuel, parking, one shared driver day

activities.note: 9-11 tastings at €25, €60, cheese dairy €12, cookery class €120, €160

profile.difficultyNote: 2/5, cellar stairs, sloping vineyard rows, two hours standing at a butcher's counter

gatewayAirport: FLR Florence Peretola, 55 min drive to Greve in Chianti; PSA Pisa 1 h 40 min; BLQ Bologna 1 h 55 min
summary: One grape, three denominations, and a 90 km transect explaining why they taste nothing alike. You start on the galestro ridges between Greve and Radda, where Chianti Classico has just redrawn itself into eleven named sub-zones; drop south to Montalcino, where Sangiovese Grosso ripens earlier and spends five years in wood; and finish among Pienza's pecorino dairies and Cortona's Etruscan terraces. Three estates a day is a hangover, two is an education. It suits people who want to leave able to taste Panzano against Lamole blind.

itinerary.title: Florence to Greve, the Gallo Nero briefing
itinerary.morning: Land at Peretola, collect the car and leave on the SR222 Chiantigiana rather than fighting Florence's ZTL, passing San Casciano where the UGA map begins.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk Greve's funnel-shaped Piazza Matteotti, then use **Le Cantine di Greve in Chianti**, a self-serve enoteca of roughly 140 wines, the cheapest way to calibrate Annata against Riserva against Gran Selezione before spending money at estates.
itinerary.evening: **Ristoro di Lamole**, up the hairpins at 550 m, for peposo and a terrace over the Lamole terraces.
itinerary.dayStats: 42 km / 55 min from FLR / 1 enoteca, 8-10 pours at €2, €6 / Annata bottle band €14, €22

itinerary.title: Panzano: the Conca d'Oro and the butcher
itinerary.morning: 8 km south to **Fontodi**, organic since the 1980s, on the floor of the Conca d'Oro amphitheatre; ask to walk out and see galestro shale in section.
itinerary.afternoon: Second estate at **Il Molino di Grace** or **Vecchie Terre di Montefili**, then the ridge path for the view that explains the UGA boundary.
itinerary.evening: **Officina della Bistecca** at Cecchini, fixed communal menu built on the bistecca, oil, salt and Dario's own Chianti. The sitting starts as one; be on time.
itinerary.dayStats: 22 km driving / 2 estates / fees €35, €50 each / Cecchini fixed menu about €60 with wine / Gran Selezione €38, €75

itinerary.title: Radda, Gaiole and the art of ageing
itinerary.morning: **Radda in Chianti** at 530 m: **Montevertine** if your email landed, otherwise **Val delle Corti** or **Poggerino**. Altitude reads as acidity and red fruit, not weight.
itinerary.afternoon: The strada bianca to **Castello di Ama**, Gaiole, San Lorenzo Gran Selezione, Vigneto Bellavista, and site-specific work by Kapoor, Kounellis and Chen Zhen through the cellars.
itinerary.evening: **Badia a Coltibuono**'s restaurant in the eleventh-century abbey for ribollita and pappardelle sul cinghiale; **Osteria Le Panzanelle** at Lucarelli is the cheaper call.
itinerary.dayStats: 55 km / 2 estates / Ama €40, €70 including the art park / 8 km white gravel, drive at 30 km/h

itinerary.title: Pici by hand, then south to Montalcino
itinerary.morning: The cookery class at **Badia a Coltibuono**: hand-rolled eggless pici, a sauce, a dessert, eaten with the abbey's wines.
itinerary.afternoon: Through **Castellina in Chianti** for the Via delle Volte tunnel-street, then the SR2 Cassia past Siena into the Val d'Orcia.
itinerary.evening: **Osticcio** in Montalcino, a wine bar over the Ombrone, a first Brunello flight and cinta senese salumi.
itinerary.dayStats: Class 4 h, €120, €160 / 78 km, 1 h 25 min Gaiole-Montalcino / Brunello by the glass €9, €16

itinerary.title: Brunello: north slope, south slope
itinerary.morning: North first, **Il Marroneto** below the walls or **Canalicchio di Sopra** at Montosoli, tasting Rosso beside Brunello to see what four extra years does.
itinerary.afternoon: South to **Sant'Angelo in Colle** for **Il Poggione** or **Argiano**, then the Romanesque **Abbazia di Sant'Antimo** below Castelnuovo dell'Abate, twelfth-century travertine that glows at 17:00.
itinerary.evening: **Il Leccio** at Sant'Angelo in Colle for pinci all'aglione. Driver day: book Sunny Tuscany Transfers or use the hotel's car.
itinerary.dayStats: 46 km / 2 estates / fees €25, €45, usually waived on two bottles / Brunello €40, €90, Riserva €70, €180, Rosso €18, €28

itinerary.title: Pienza pecorino and Montepulciano's Nobile
itinerary.morning: Across the Val d'Orcia to **Pienza**, Pius II's Renaissance grid town, and **Podere Il Casale** or **Caseificio Cugusi** for the pecorino sequence: fresco, semi-stagionato, stagionato, then the leaf- and ash-aged wheels.
itinerary.afternoon: **Montepulciano** at 605 m: Vino Nobile at biodynamic **Avignonesi** at Valiano, or the medieval cellars of **Contucci** and **De' Ricci** under Piazza Grande, among the few here that tolerate short notice.
itinerary.evening: **La Grotta**, opposite San Biagio, or **Osteria Acquacheta** for bistecca priced by the etto.
itinerary.dayStats: 62 km / 1 dairy + 2 cellars / cheese tasting €10, €15 / Vino Nobile €18, €35, Pieve €35, €60

itinerary.title: Cortona, the oil mill, and out
itinerary.morning: East to **Cortona**, Etruscan walls above the Valdichiana, for the MAEC museum's bronze lamp. Cortona DOC is Syrah country, a useful palate reset.
itinerary.afternoon: **Frantoio Pruneti** at San Polo in Chianti for a guided oil tasting, or, in November, a live pressing, then hand the car back at Peretola.
itinerary.evening: **Trattoria Cammillo** or **Il Santo Bevitore** in Florence if you fly the next morning.
itinerary.dayStats: 115 km Montalcino-Cortona-Florence / oil tasting €12, €20 / DOP Chianti Classico oil 500 ml €18, €26 / allow 2 h to the airport

accommodationStrategy.name: Villa Bordoni
accommodationStrategy.description: On a dirt lane 4 km from Greve, putting Panzano, Lamole and Radda inside 25 minutes. Free parking, a real cellar list, and a kitchen that still feeds you after a late Gaiole finish. €220, €340 double B&B.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Vecchia Oliviera
accommodationStrategy.description: Just outside Porta Cerbaia with its own car park, two minutes from Osticcio and the Fortezza enoteca, west-facing over the Val d'Orcia. Best value for the Brunello days at €150, €220 double.

accommodationStrategy.name: Castello di Velona
accommodationStrategy.description: The splurge: an eleventh-century castle above Sant'Antimo with thermal pools, isolated enough to force the driver arrangement the week needs anyway. €350, €600 double.

logistics.connectivity: EU roaming, no surcharge. 4G is reliable in towns, patchy on the strade bianche between Radda and Gaiole. Download offline maps, several estate entrances are unsigned gates with a number.
logistics.emergency: 112. Nearest hospitals are Campostaggia (Poggibonsi) for Chianti and Nottola (Montepulciano) for the Val d'Orcia. EHIC/GHIC accepted; add rental-excess cover.
logistics.weather: Hail between mid-May and July is the real hazard and closes roads fast. September afternoons still reach 30°C.
logistics.bookingWindows: Cecchini's Officina 4-8 weeks; Biondi-Santi and Montevertine 6-12 weeks; Ama and Antinori 2-4 weeks; Coltibuono classes 3-4 weeks. Small Montalcino estates answer Italian email faster than English.
logistics.money: Eurozone. Cards near-universal, but frantoi, dairies and farm stands prefer cash; carry €150. Service is normally included, round up. The €2, €4 coperto is not a tip.
logistics.transportRules: Florence, Siena, Montalcino and Montepulciano enforce **ZTL** camera zones; fines arrive months later via the rental company, so park outside the walls always. Rural fuel stations close 13:00-15:30 and Sundays, though most have unattended card pumps. Autostrada tolls pay at the barrier.
logistics.permits: Tasting fees of €25, €60 are standard and often credited against two to six bottles, ask when booking, not at the till. Intra-EU shipping is simple; UK and US runs €30, €90 a case plus duty.
logistics.health: Tap water is drinkable, fountains included. The blood-alcohol limit of 0.50 g/l is less than one tasting flight, use the spittoons and treat the driver rota as fixed. Ticks in woodland edges April-October.

proTips: Ask every Gran Selezione producer which UGA is on the label and why. That tier is the only one permitted to name a sub-zone, so it is the only bottle that tells you where in Chianti Classico you actually are.
Taste Rosso di Montalcino beside Brunello at the same estate. Identical fruit, four years apart, more education in ten minutes than a vertical costing five times as much.
Book Cecchini's lunch counter instead of dinner if you are driving. Dario DOC plus a glass costs a fraction of the Officina and leaves you sober by 15:00.
Estates on the Radda-Gaiole gravel open on the hour and do not wait. Arrive five minutes early or lose the slot to tomorrow.
Late October is the sweet spot: harvest done so owners will talk, mills running, vineyard colour at peak. Late September fails all three tests.
Buy oil at the frantoio, not the estate. November olio nuovo under a DOP Chianti Classico seal is a different product from supermarket Toscano IGP, and the price gap is narrower than you think.
Enoteca La Fortezza inside Montalcino's fortress pours four producers' Brunello side by side for the cost of one estate visit, use it on arrival to decide which two estates to book.
Ship, don't carry. Two cases of Brunello break most baggage allowances, and estate shippers handle the paperwork better than a courier found later.

raw.Chianti Classico DOCG: , minimum 80% Sangiovese; Gran Selezione since the 2023 revision requires 90% and bans international varieties. Tiers: Annata (12 months), Riserva (24 months), Gran Selezione (30 months, estate fruit only). The eleven **UGA** sub-zones, San Casciano, Montefioralle, Panzano, Lamole, Greve, Radda, Gaiole, Castellina, Vagliagli, Castelnuovo Berardenga, San Donato in Poggio, may be printed **only on Gran Selezione labels**. Lamole at 500-650 m on sandstone gives floral, high-toned wine; Panzano's Conca d'Oro gives grip; Castelnuovo Berardenga is warmest and roundest.
raw.Brunello di Montalcino DOCG: , 100% Sangiovese Grosso, 4 years' ageing (2 in oak), released 1 January of the fifth year; Riserva 5 years. **Rosso di Montalcino DOC** is the same fruit at one year and is the sane weekday drinking; **Sant'Antimo DOC** covers the rest. North slope (Montosoli, Torrenieri) is perfumed; Sant'Angelo in Colle in the south ripens hardest. **Vino Nobile di Montepulciano DOCG**, 70% minimum Sangiovese, locally Prugnolo Gentile, 24 months; the new **Pieve** tier needs 85% from twelve named parish districts. **Bolgheri DOC** is the coastal outlier: Cabernet and Merlot on beach gravel.
raw.Reservation-only estates: Nobody takes weekday walk-ins. **Castello di Ama** (Gaiole; San Lorenzo Gran Selezione plus a contemporary art park) books via castellodiama.com, roughly €40, €70, English standard, 3-4 weeks ahead. **Antinori nel Chianti Classico** at Bargino sells timed online tours, €45, €75. **Fontodi** (Panzano) answers email, two weeks' notice, €35, €50 usually credited against a case. **Montevertine** (Radda) takes very few visitors, email only, 6-8 weeks. In Montalcino, **Biondi-Santi Tenuta Greppo** books months ahead at €80, €150 for verticals; **Il Marroneto**, **Poggio di Sotto** and **Salvioni** are email-only; **Argiano** and **Il Poggione** reply within days.
raw.Producers beyond wine: **Antica Macelleria Cecchini**, Via XX Luglio 11, Panzano, Dario Cecchini's butcher shop and three eating rooms: Officina della Bistecca (fixed, about €60, communal, one sitting), Solociccia (€35, €40), and the Dario DOC burger counter at lunch; book on dariocecchini.com. **Caseificio Cugusi**, Via della Boccia 8, Montepulciano, and **Podere Il Casale** above Pienza for Pecorino di Pienza aged in ash, walnut leaves or hay, €10, €15. **Frantoio Pruneti** at San Polo presses Moraiolo, Frantoio and Leccino. **Forno Lombardi** (Greve) for unsalted pane sciocco.
raw.Harvest timing: Chianti Classico picks roughly 15 September-10 October; Montalcino starts a week earlier. The last week of September is the worst week for an owner's attention and the best for seeing a crushpad, choose. **Olive pressing runs 25 October-late November** and is the most rewarding hands-on window.
raw.Hands-on element: A half-day pici and sauce class in the abbey kitchen at **Badia a Coltibuono**, Gaiole, €120, €160 with lunch and estate wine, English-taught, 3-4 weeks' notice. In November swap it for a dawn pressing at Frantoio Pruneti, following your own crate through the mill.
raw.Designated-driver strategy: Italy's limit is 0.50 g/l, and zero for licences under three years old. Chianti has no useful public transport. Budget two driver days: **Tuscany Wine Tours by Massimo** and **Grape Tours Florence** run English-speaking drivers at roughly €450, €600 per car per day for 2-4 people; **Sunny Tuscany Transfers** covers the Montalcino leg. Trains only help at the edges, Florence SMN-Siena 1 h 30 m, Chiusi-Chianciano for Montepulciano plus a 20-minute taxi.

sources.verified: The eleven Chianti Classico UGA sub-zones and the rule restricting UGA names to Gran Selezione labels, plus Gran Selezione's 90% Sangiovese minimum and exclusion of international varieties; Castello di Ama's public visiting page; Antinori nel Chianti Classico's online timed-tour booking; Dario Cecchini's own site listing Officina della Bistecca, Solociccia and Dario in Panzano as distinct bookable formats.
sources.confidenceNotes: Tasting fees are indicative bands, not confirmed 2026 list prices, re-check Ama, Antinori, Fontodi and Biondi-Santi directly. Cecchini's fixed-menu price and sitting times shift seasonally. Montevertine's visitor policy is restrictive and may be closed entirely in any period. Badia a Coltibuono's class calendar varies by month, confirm before fixing Day 4. The Vino Nobile Pieve district list is still settling. Hotel rates are prior-season estimates.
